summary: The pyrolisk's AD_FIRE gaze at step 138 completes first. On step 139 the shopkeeper selects MUSE_WAN_STRIKING. C muse.c:use_offensive() passes zap.c:bhito as mbhit's floor-object callback; the source path reaches dothrow.c:breaks()/breaktest() and zap.c:obj_resists(), consuming two rn2(100) draws on floor objects. The existing JS js/muse.js:use_offensive() passes null for that callback and records note_unported('zap.c bhito'), so both object-resistance draws are skipped; the next JS draw is rn2(5)=2 from distfleeck(). This is a bounded callback-wiring divergence fix in the existing offensive wand arm, not a claim that use_offensive() or bhito() is newly ported in full.

source.branch: The shared MUSE_WAN_TELEPORTATION, MUSE_WAN_UNDEAD_TURNING, and MUSE_WAN_STRIKING wand arm calls mbhit(mtmp, rn1(8, 6), mbhitm, bhito, otmp). For the admitted case's MUSE_WAN_STRIKING selection, JS currently passes null in the bhito callback slot and records zap.c bhito as unported. Restore the existing bhito callback at this source-aligned mbhit call; keep use_offensive and bhito completion credit unchanged.
callers: muse.c:use_offensive -> mbhit -> fhito_loc -> zap.c:bhito(WAN_STRIKING) -> dothrow.c:breaks/breaktest -> zap.c:obj_resists
dependencies: zap.c:bhito (existing JS implementation js/zap.js; callback-compatible mbhit input)
zap.c:obj_resists (existing JS implementation js/bury.js; source helper used by floor-object resistance checks)

evidence: The admitted baseline reports the first mismatch at segment 0 step 139: C rn2(100)=52 @ obj_resists(zap.c:1469), JS rn2(5)=2; screen and cursor diverge at step 140.

C nethack-c/upstream/src/muse.c:1844-1889 routes the MUSE_WAN_STRIKING wand through mbhit(mtmp, rn1(8, 6), mbhitm, bhito, otmp). C zap.c:2119-2427 defines bhito's WAN_STRIKING floor-object path, which calls the existing dothrow break checks; that path reaches obj_resists at zap.c:1469.

JS js/muse.js:2694-2705 groups the same three wand types but calls mbhit(..., mbhitm, null, ...), preceded by note_unported('zap.c bhito'). The complete existing js/zap.js:bhito implementation accepts the callback signature expected by js/zap.js:mbhit and already owns the floor-object branches.

The immutable admitted recipe identifies the case as polyself.c:dogaze followed by muse.c:use_offensive1884 -> mbhit1734 -> fhito_loc -> zap.c:bhito WAN_STRIKING -> dothrow.c:breaks/breaktest -> obj_resists. The step-138 gaze is not the source of the first mismatch; the first missing draws occur on the following shopkeeper wand action.
